propositions: A configured provider is silently dropped for any model id containing a colon because _resolve_target's 'already-qualified' test is 'if ":" in model', which canonical versioned Bedrock ids (…-v1:0) satisfy for the wrong reason.
The dropped-provider failure surfaces late as a misleading 'unknown provider' error that names a fragment of the model id, contradicting the operator's actual provider = "bedrock" configuration.

infer_provider and _resolve_target were two independent colon-based implementations of the same question and failed the same way; they are unified into one split_provider_qualifier helper with a test asserting they agree.
The fix must honour a configured provider for colon-bearing ids, never double-prefix already-qualified strings, and keep every existing unqualified id resolving byte-for-byte unchanged.

Silent fallback to a default provider is explicitly rejected because Bedrock is chosen for data-residency/contractual reasons; the gate must fail closed and fail fast rather than substitute a different provider.

Guard order is the core fix: a configured provider must short-circuit before any qualifier scan, and a conflicting inline qualifier raises LLMConfigError, closing a second silent-drop hole (e.g. _resolve_target('openai:gpt-4o', 'bedrock')).
